blocks.value: Information hiding restricts access to parts of an object. A public instance variable or method can be used from anywhere; a private one can only be used inside its own class's definition.
Information hiding makes code easier to understand and use, simplifies fixing and modifying it, and makes it easier to reuse.
Two common types of methods work around private data: an accessor (a public method that returns a private instance variable's value) and a mutator (a public method that changes it).
Encapsulation is the practice this enables: bundling instance variables and methods together into a class, and hiding the implementation details behind public methods like accessors and mutators.
A UML class diagram is a standard way to sketch a class's structure: the class name on top, its variables below that, and its methods at the bottom.
